messages:
Mia (support): heads-up — customer ACME reported that our tool router picked the wrong tool during a function call. They asked the model to schedule a pickup but the runtime invoked the 'place_order' tool instead, which created a duplicate order. Customer is blocked and upset.

Mia (support): reproduction summary: 1) customer sends chat completion with tool set that includes 'place_order.v2' and 'schedule_pickup.v1' 2) model returns a tool_choice for 'place_order.v2' 3) platform executes it (we do not block) -> duplicate order created.

Mia (support): minimal request body they used (redacted keys):
```json
{"model":"redwood-chat-1-tool","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Please schedule a pickup for order #12345 tomorrow at 10am."}],"tools":[{"name":"place_order","version":"v2","description":"Create a new order","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"sku":{"type":"string"},"qty":{"type":"integer"},"delivery_time":{"type":"string"},"customer_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["sku","qty","customer_id"]}},{"name":"schedule_pickup","version":"v1","description":"Schedule pickup for an existing order","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"},"pickup_time":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id","pickup_time"]}}],"temperature":0}
```

Mia (support): model response (as we received it) — note it selected place_order and passed arguments with order id missing but customer id present (because customer asked loosely):
```json
{"tool_choice":"place_order","arguments":{"sku":"widget-001","qty":1,"customer_id":"cust-987"}}
```

Mia (support): expected tool_choice -> schedule_pickup with arguments {"order_id":"12345","pickup_time":"2026-03-16T10:00:00Z"}.

Jason (eng): thanks, this looks like a classic ambiguity between tool metadata and how the model prefers tokens. The two tools both have the substring "order" (place_order vs schedule_pickup's description mentions "order") — model is biased to emit place_order because it has a broader parameter set and the customer phrased things in natural language without 'order_id'.

Jason (eng): quick theory: model selects tool based on token-level heuristics + schema fit. Because place_order's schema accepts customer_id and has more required fields, the model may have decided it can fulfill intent by creating a new order. Our router then executed it because we allow model-initiated tool calls.

Elaine (platform): can you paste the tool-manifest metadata we pass into the router? I want to check name/id fields and if we index description text anywhere.

Mia (support): pasted above in the code block. note: tool objects only have name, version, description, parameters as shown. No explicit unique id beyond name+version.

Jason (eng): reproduce steps for us to run locally — thanks. I'm going to run a couple of experiments: 1) force model to call schedule_pickup by adding a required 'order_id' in the user prompt, 2) force function_call explicit name and see if router obeys, 3) run our schema-matcher to see matching scores.

Jason (eng): quick local log from my experiment:
```
[2026-03-16T15:02:11Z] request id=abc123 model=redwood-chat-1-tool prompt="schedule pickup for order 12345"
[2026-03-16T15:02:12Z] model_tool_choice=place_order score=0.62
[2026-03-16T15:02:12Z] schema_match(schedule_pickup)=0.48 schema_match(place_order)=0.51
[2026-03-16T15:02:12Z] router executed place_order -> created order id new-445
```

Jason (eng): so the numeric schema_match shows place_order slightly higher. That's enough to select the wrong tool. We need disambiguation rules.

Mia (support): customer impact: duplicated orders for 3 customers so far, billing team flagged 2 refunds. Could be more if not patched.

Elaine (platform): mitigation options (short-term):
- Turn on a conservative router mode for affected tenants: prefer exact name match when user explicitly mentions 'schedule' or 'pickup'.
- Add a temporary block that prevents place_order from auto-executing if the prompt mentions an order_id pattern ("#\d+"), instead require explicit confirmation.
- Suggest customers use function_call explicit name in their client until we ship fix.

Jason (eng): long-term fix ideas:
- Enhance tool-router scoring to heavily weight semantic match of 'operation intent' and penalize creation actions if user mentions existing order identifiers.
- Require tool manifests include an immutable 'tool_id' and 'intent_tags' (e.g., ["create","schedule"]) so the model and router can reason with structured meta instead of free-text descriptions.
- Add regression tests that exercise ambiguous pairs (create vs modify vs schedule).

Jason (eng): I'll open PR branch fix/tool-router-disambiguation with two changes: 1) change scoring to +0.25 boost for explicit token matches like 'schedule'/'pickup' vs 'place'/'create' (config flag), 2) add a safety check that will reject executing a create action if the user prompt contains an order id pattern unless the model returned explicit confirmation. Will canary to 5% of requests for now.

Mia (support): can you also add a telemetry tag so we can surface all past executions where place_order executed within 30s of a user mentioning order_id? I'd like a list to contact affected customers.

Jason (eng): yes — adding log tag router.disambiguation_hint and a query metric. ETA for canary: ~3 hours after PR merge. Full rollout after 24h monitoring if no false negatives.

Elaine (platform): action items: Jason -> PR + canary config, Mia -> gather list of affected customers and their request ids, Platform -> temporary conservative routing for ACME tenant (applied).

Mia (support): assigning follow-ups: I've DM'd ACME with an apology and a temporary workaround (use explicit function_call with name). ACME accepted rollback of the duplicate order and account-level conservative routing.

Jason (eng): I'll also add a unit test that asserts schedule_pickup is chosen for prompts containing 'pickup' and an order id.

Mia (support): thx all. tagging @bot-toolrouter for audit logs :eyes:

bot-toolrouter: audit log recorded event router.choice=place_order request_id=abc123 timestamp=2026-03-16T15:02:12Z

Mia (support): marking this thread as escalation -> eng bug. I'll update ACME once we have canary live and a cleanup plan for refunds.

Jason (eng): will post PR link when ready.

Elaine (platform): noted. please paste PR and canary link here and the customer list.

Mia (support): will do — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
